newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Aiwa Singapore to take on managerial role.
newsitem.headline: Aiwa Singapore to take on managerial role.

text.p: Aiwa Co Ltd's Singapore output contribution to the group was projected to fall from its peak of 10 percent to five percent in fiscal year 1997 as it assumes a managerial role, Aiwa's president said on Tuesday.

"At its peak, Singapore production was at 10 percent of the total Aiwa group output. For the year ending March 31 1997, it is estimated this will be reduced to five percent," Yoshio Ishigaki told a news briefing.
"The strategy from now is for Aiwa Singapore to take on a new managerial role to concentrate on supporting regional production bases, procurement and sourcing of cheaper parts," he said.
Singapore will also oversee product distribution as well as support the group's regional expansion, he said.
Over the past years, the company has reduced production at its Jurong factory, located on the western part of Singapore, to three lines from 14.
Ishigaki said the production facilities in Jurong will gradually be transferred to lower cost countries like Indonesia.
Singapore, together with Japan, will be a centre providing technical support to production bases.
However, Singapore and Japan would still produce higher-end products like MiniDisc and Digital Video Disc, Ishigaki said.
He added no further staff lay-offs were expected in Singapore. Last year, some workers were laid off after Aiwa cut its production at Jurong.
Aiwa is a unit of Sony Corp.
